carrierRelationship.note: Identity 7a — the control principal per (relationship × carrier). Ed25519-only; no key-agreement key exists for this class. info = prefix || Dc || Dn, both digests exactly 47 ASCII characters (length-fixed, so the split point is positional).
carrierRelationship.relationshipNonceNote: documented sample, deterministic for this vector set (sha2-256 of the ASCII label "rltp/vector/carrier-relationship/nonce-1"). A real carrier nonce MUST come from a CSPRNG, is its own register entry, is NEVER the pair-label nonce of Identity 6.1, and never travels.

cases.case: the SAME relationship at a second carrier — one nonce, two unrelated principals (Identity 7a.3)
byte-exactness (Identity 7a.2): a case variant of carrier A's string is a DIFFERENT carrier — no case folding, no normalization

identifierGrammar.note: Identity 7a.2 — the ordered validation pipeline for C. Valid Unicode scalar values (no surrogates, never repaired), NO normalization step (the deliberate difference to 6.2), 1..1024 UTF-8 bytes, no Cc/Cf/White_Space code point anywhere. Validation runs before the UTF-8 bytes enter Dc.

rejects.reason: interior White_Space — an invisible difference must not name a second carrier
lone surrogate — rejected, never replaced by U+FFFD (given as a JSON escape because the value is not encodable as UTF-8, which is the point)

identifierGrammar.nfcNote: The NFC and NFD spellings of one name are BOTH valid and are TWO carriers — no normalization is applied. This is the case 6.2 decides the other way for persona names, and the two spellings MUST derive two different principals.

unicodePin.note: Identity 7a.2 step 4 — the pinned property sets, shipped as data so the Unicode 15.0 pin is executed rather than delegated to whatever tables a runtime happens to carry. A conforming implementation MUST evaluate step 4 against these ranges; where its platform disagrees, these govern.
unicodePin.provenance: Generated from Python unicodedata (Unicode 15.1 tables, which are identical to 15.0 for both properties) and cross-checked against a Node 22 / ICU 77 (Unicode 16.0) enumeration: both agree range for range. Cc needs no table and is given for completeness.

rawByteRejects.reason: overlong two-byte encoding of U+002F — a strict UTF-8 decode MUST fail, never yield '/'
stray continuation byte with no lead
surrogate U+D800 encoded as UTF-8 (CESU-8 style) — not a scalar value
five-byte sequence — no such thing in UTF-8
well-formed UTF-8 but carries U+0000 (Cc) — rejected at step 4, not step 1

rawByteAccepts.reason: did:web:carrier.example as raw bytes — decodes and passes every step

carrierRelationship.secondRelationshipNonceNote: documented sample, deterministic for this vector set (sha2-256 of the ASCII label "rltp/vector/carrier-relationship/nonce-2"). Its purpose is the axis the first three cases do not exercise: they vary C and hold N, this varies N and holds C.

relationshipAxisCase.case: the SAME carrier, a second relationship nonce — one carrier, two unrelated principals (the counter-vector to the three carrier cases)

nonceConvergence.note: Identity §7a.3 — a register entry is {nonce, generation}. Canonical = highest generation; ties by unsigned bytewise-smallest nonce. Entries are superseded, never deleted, so a re-appearing older entry is harmless without a tombstone. Only the nonce enters the derivation.

cases.case: concurrent first writes — two devices, same generation: the bytes decide (the round-2 case, unchanged)
deliberate rotation — the new nonce sorts HIGHER and must still win, which bytewise-smallest alone could not deliver
the superseded entry re-appears after a partition heal or a restore from an older state copy — it carries the lower generation and stays superseded
two devices rotate concurrently to the same generation — a race again, settled by the bytes at that generation

nonceConvergence.neverDeleted: A device MUST retain a superseded entry. Case 3 is the reason: deleting it would make its re-appearance new information again.

generationDomain.note: Identity 7a.3 — generation is an integer in [1, 2^53-1], canonical JSON integer form (no sign, no leading zero, no fraction, no exponent). The bound is the largest integer every JSON implementation represents exactly: beyond it a double-based runtime cannot tell two generations apart and would read a rotation as a tie, while an arbitrary-precision one would not. Out-of-domain entries are INVALID and rejected, never clamped.

rejects.reason: below the domain — generations start at 1
2^53 — outside the domain; this is exactly where a double-based runtime stops distinguishing successive integers
2^53+1 — indistinguishable from 2^53 in IEEE-754, which is the divergence the domain forbids
leading zero — not the canonical integer form

boundaryCase.case: a rotation at the top of the domain still resolves by generation, not by bytes
boundaryCase.note: n2 sorts HIGHER than n1, so a bytewise-only rule would pick n1; the generation decides. Both values are exactly representable, which is the point of the bound.

carrierRelationship.keyAgreementNote: Identity 7a.1 — this class is Ed25519-only: NO key-agreement key is derived, and the null is here so a runner can assert the absence instead of the spec merely announcing it. Sealing stays at the rkid of 5.2; a carrier-relationship principal signs and authenticates and receives nothing.
